analysis:
Integration of the five source passes plus replayed patches. All changes are CI tooling and documentation: .github/workflows/darkbloom-watchdog.yml, changelog.d/darkbloom-watchdog-listing-size.md, docs/developer/build.md (head ~437-454) and scripts/test-darkbloom-route.py (comment at line 132, new assertion ~949-953). None touches the provider runtime, the coordinator WebSocket contract (TB-002), operator/process boundary (TB-003), inference engine or prefix cache (TB-007, T-041), attestation (TB-009), App Attest authorization (TB-011), the add-on hold socket (TB-012), the installer (TB-013) or the GPU limit (TB-014). Provider assets A-001 through A-020 are not affected.

Workflow behavior: runs_with/jobs_of now write each page to files under the mktemp dir and merge via `jq -cs 'add // []'`. Previously listings were passed as `--argjson`, which overflowed argv ('Argument list too long'). API JSON goes through files or stdin and is not interpolated into shell commands, so no injection surface is added. Error semantics are preserved: a non-200 status returns 1 and callers still warn and exit. The stranded predicate is now timed from each Darkbloom job's own created_at and is suppressed only if a Darkbloom job got a runner within the wait. Effect: a run with a single stranded shard is rescued, and jobs waiting by design at a payer limit can be cancelled and re-run on fallback runners. This is an availability and policy tradeoff that is explicitly disclosed in the comments, docs and changelog. It is bounded by at-most-once rescue, the minutes validation, the marker check and a token limited to actions:write and checks:write. Permissions, token handling and the API host check are unchanged.

The test addition only constrains workflow text (a regex heuristic) and weakens no existing guard. Limits: the upstream template at d6d257c2 'copied unchanged' cannot be verified from the evidence, and omitted replay units exist (12). This is a provenance question, not a demonstrated security regression. No findings.
